papers.title: Adversarial Wronskians: A proof of the Kung--Traub conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Kung--Traub conjecture: a deterministic stationary root-finding method without memory, using at most $n$ real scalar function or derivative evaluations per iteration, cannot have local order greater than $2^{n-1}$ on every real analytic function with a simple zero. For $n\geq2$, the bound is attained by the methods of Kung and Traub. The local estimate is required at every sufficiently close starting point, with constants that may depend on the function. Evaluation points and derivative orders may be chosen adaptively, and the rules for choosing them and processing the data are unrestricted. The proof uses a localisation property of polynomial Wronskians to obtain a lower bound at each fixed scale. A diagonal construction then gives one entire function, with derivative bounded above and below on the real line, for which every larger order fails. We also obtain a sharper bound when evaluations are made in prescribed groups, and prove the corresponding result for complex scalar evaluations. The results of this paper are also formally verified in Lean.

papers.title: Sharp Nonlocal Poincar\'e Inequalities and Liminf Lower Bounds for Sobolev and BV Energies on Metric Measure Spaces
papers.abstract: Let $p\in[1,\infty)$, and let $(X,\rho,\mu)$ be a complete doubling $q$-Poincar\'e space for some $q\in[1,p]$ with a lower dimension $d$ and an upper dimension $D$. In this article, we establish Poincar\'e inequalities for two families of nonlocal nonconvex functionals defined using distances or volumes. More precisely, for any ball $B$ with its radius $r_B\in(0,\operatorname{diam} X)$, any $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, and any measurable function $f:X\to\mathbb R$, \begin{align*} &\frac{1}{\mu(B)^2}\int_B\int_B|f(x)-f(y)|^p\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y)\\ &\quad\lesssim\lambda^pr_B^p\phi(B)^{\gamma p}+\frac{\lambda^pr_B^p}{\mu(B)}\mathop{\int_{\Lambda B}\int_{\Lambda B}}\limits_{\genfrac{}{}{}{2}{|f(x)-f(y)|}{\rho(x,y)\phi(x,y)^\gamma}>\lambda}\frac{\phi(x,y)^{\gamma p}}{V(x,y)}\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y), \end{align*} where $V(x,y):=\mu(B(x,\rho(x,y)))$ and either $\phi=\rho$ with $\phi(B)=r_B$ and $\gamma\in(-\infty,-\frac{\min\{q,D\}}{p}]$ or $\phi=V$ with $\phi(B)=\mu(B)$ and $\gamma\in(-\infty,-\frac{q}{p\max\{q,d\}}]$. Here both ranges of $\gamma$ are sharp over the class of $q$-Poincar\'e spaces with the prescribed lower and upper dimensions, and the constant $\Lambda\in[1,\infty)$ and the implicit positive constant depend only on $p$, $\gamma$, and the geometric constants of $X$. We also obtain lower bounds for Sobolev energy and total variation in terms of the limit inferior of these functionals, for $\gamma$ in either the above negative ranges or $(0,\infty)$. Our proofs use the curve characterization of Poincar\'e spaces and an adaptive dyadic refinement argument based on medians.

papers.title: Local Smoothing Estimates of Schr\"{o}dinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
papers.abstract: We establish improved local smoothing estimates for the Schr\"odinger equation on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.

papers.title: Simple proofs of a Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality and their extensions
papers.abstract: We revisit the one-dimensional Gagliardo-Nirenberg interpolation inequality $$\|u'\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R})}\leq C\|u\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R})}^{1-a}\|u''\|_{L^r(\mathbb{R})}^{a},\qquad u\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}),\quad \tfrac12\leq a\leq 1,$$ and recall how its general form follows from the case $a=\frac12$ by interpolation with an endpoint estimate. For $a=\frac12$ and $p=q=r$, we give four alternative proofs, based on integration by parts (two proofs), on an ODE, and on the $L^p$ theory of singular integrals. The two proofs by integration by parts also cover most of the other admissible exponents. In $\mathbb{R}^N$, the integration by parts arguments give the inequality with explicit constants and, for $p\leq 2$, with the Laplacian in place of the Hessian and a constant independent of the dimension. For weighted measures $w(x)\,dx$, a pointwise version of the ODE argument gives the pointwise inequality $|\nabla u|^2\leq C_N\,Mu\,M(\Delta u)$, where $M$ is the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function, and hence the inequality for Muckenhoupt weights, with the Laplacian and an explicit constant. The integration by parts arguments give it for homogeneous weights of large degree and for superharmonic weights. These results apply, in particular, to power weights and to monomial weights.

papers.title: Sharp convex body sparse bounds and quantitative matrix weighted estimates for Hilbert transforms along curves
papers.abstract: We prove convex body sparse bounds for coordinatewise Hilbert transforms along monomial curves and local $C^d$ curves with uniformly nonvanishing torsion on the closed integration interval. Adapting the scalar estimates of Cladek--Ou \cite{CladekOu2018} and the lifting method of Laukkarinen--Lorist \cite{LaukkarinenLorist2026} to the anisotropic geometry, we obtain one sparse family of genuine curve-adapted boxes and quantitative $L^p(W)$ bounds for matrix weights. The convex body sparse exponent range is sharp up to its boundary: estimates hold in the interior of $\Omega_d$, while any fixed finite number of sparse families fails outside $\overline{\Omega_d}$ when $1/r+1/s>1$. We also establish an explicit endpoint-contact obstruction. For every interior planar exponent pair, a polynomial curve with positive torsion on the open integration interval violates the full-interval sparse estimate.

papers.title: The full shadow of a polynomial II. Vanishing root masses and holes
papers.abstract: For a complex polynomial $P$, its full shadow is the closure of the set of zeros of all derivatives of all powers $P^n$, and its limiting core is the Hausdorff limit, as $n\to\infty$, of the set of zeros of all derivatives of $P^n$. These sets retain geometric information that weak limits of root-counting measures discard. We determine complete zero-set limits for arrays of polynomials whose roots approach finitely many locations. A cluster containing $o(D)$ roots of a degree-$D$ polynomial can survive outside the limiting support of the derivative zeros, which depends only on the positive limiting masses: under repeated differentiation, the zeros it produces follow a straight path, selected by an explicit min--max condition, and preserve the cluster's exact multiplicity. When such a location instead carries a small positive mass $\varepsilon$, the support of the limiting zero distribution at a fixed ratio of derivative order to degree develops an arc on the $\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ scale with a universal local semicircle profile. We use these mechanisms to prove that polynomial shadows can have robust and arbitrarily complicated topology. For every $k\ge2$, there are polynomials with $k+2$ distinct root locations whose limiting cores and full shadows have at least $\binom{k}{2}$ holes; this persists under coefficient perturbations and among square-free polynomials without a reflection axis. In a four-location family, the core and full-shadow areas tend to zero while one hole has area tending to $8/1221$.

papers.title: Dilation systems with two generators and the optimal Riesz bounds of a basis of ReLU networks
papers.abstract: For two $1$-periodic functions $\psi_1,\psi_2\in L^2(0,1)$ with mean zero we characterize when $\{1\}\cup\{\psi_1(\alpha\cdot x),\psi_2(\alpha\cdot x)\}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}^d,\,\alpha\succ0}$ is a Riesz basis of $L^2([0,1]^d)$, in terms of a $2\times2$ matrix of Dirichlet series, and we compute its optimal bounds. The tool is a $2\times2$ matrix version of the theorem of Hedenmalm, Lindqvist and Seip for systems of dilations with two generators, proved through the reproducing kernel of the Hardy space of the infinite polydisk. In particular, we get the optimal bounds $2/3$ and $3/2$ for $\psi_1,\psi_2$ the triangle waves considered by Daubechies, DeVore, Foucart, Hanin and Petrova in $L^2(0,1)$, and the extended version in $L^2([0,1]^d)$ defined by Schneider and Vyb\'iral.

papers.title: Product Pitt inequalities and signed Boas equivalences for general monotone functions
papers.abstract: We prove product-weight Pitt inequalities for real or complex functions on $\mathbb R^d$ whose full mixed Vitali variation satisfies an exterior-tail general monotonicity condition. A two-parameter condition gives spatial weights with different powers near the coordinate hyperplanes and at infinity. For the classical parameters, a reverse estimate yields a Boas norm equivalence without sign, parity or separability assumptions. The equivalence holds for finite spatial norm and, for $L^1$ data, characterizes finiteness of either norm; the unrestricted nonintegrable converse remains open. We also prove an equivalence under primitive control, give explicit examples, and establish sharpness of the Fourier-side exponent range.

papers.title: Ullman--Stahl--Totik regularity for conjugacy measures
papers.abstract: We consider probability measures whose distribution functions solve conjugate equations between two compatible systems of increasing maps on the unit interval. We give sufficient conditions for Ullman--Stahl--Totik regularity in terms of finite compositions of the source maps and a lower mass estimate which holds at Lebesgue almost every point. Our result substantially extends a regularity theorem of Mantica and Totik by allowing nonlinear target maps and replacing their assumptions on convexity, concavity, and displacement near fixed points. The proof uses the mass criterion of Stahl and Totik from logarithmic potential theory. We give further sufficient conditions involving uniform mesh bounds, sets where derivatives equal one, and endpoint drift. Examples distinguish these conditions and show that the uniform version of the lower mass estimate can fail for regular conjugacy measures.

papers.title: Truncated Dirichlet estimates for Bloch functions
papers.abstract: We study the truncated Dirichlet functional \[ \Phi_n (f) = \sum_{k = 1}^n k |a_k|^2, \quad f(z) = \sum_{k = 0}^\infty a_k z^k, \] when $f$ belongs to the Bloch space. If $n \geq 27$, we find a normalized Bloch function $f_n$ such that \[ \Phi_n (f_n) > n B_n^2, \] where $B_n = \max \{ |a_n| : \| f \|_{\mathcal{B}} = 1 \}$, thus proving that an inequality by Kayumov and Wirths cannot be extended to large values of $n$. Nevertheless, we show that the inequality $\Phi_n(f) \leq n B_n^2$ holds for all normalized functions when $n \leq 9$.

papers.title: Elliptic Fekete points: separation, Riesz energies, and polynomial conditioning
papers.abstract: Elliptic Fekete configurations minimize logarithmic energy on the sphere. They also provide a natural source of complex polynomials with controlled Shub--Smale condition number. The link between these two problems is the product of the distances from each point to all the other points: logarithmic energy controls the geometric mean of these products, whereas local conditioning depends on each product separately. This paper studies the passage from global information to uniform estimates at individual nodes, exploring its connections with quantitative equidistribution, Riesz energies, and polynomial conditioning. We improve separation bounds for elliptic Fekete configurations and obtain quantitative Riesz-energy estimates for both these configurations and spherical roots of polynomials with optimal-order global conditioning. For $0<s<2$, these estimates also improve explicit upper bounds for the minimal Riesz $s$-energy.

papers.title: Tiling without a subspace complement: a sharp counterexample in dimension nine over the field with two elements
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit 64-point subset of $\mathbb F_2^9$ which tiles by translation but has no linear-subspace tiling complement. Together with our earlier dimension-eight theorem and a product argument, this shows that every nonempty tile in $\mathbb F_2^d$ has a linear-subspace complement precisely when $d\le8$. The example is spectral, so it is not a counterexample to Fuglede's conjecture. Its construction uses six three-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb F_2^6$, specified by a small table. We classify all its tiling complements and spectra: there are exactly 512 complements and 64 spectra, with one translation class of each. Every spectrum has normalized Wiener norm $15/8$. An appendix proves that Goyal's related construction is affinely inequivalent but has the same tiling complements and spectra. The construction and both classifications are proved from first principles. We also give elementary proofs of the positive assertion in dimensions at most seven and for all tile sizes other than sixteen in dimension eight. The remaining case uses our previously established theorem based on the classification of perfect binary codes of length fifteen.

papers.title: Asymmetric $L^p$-improving and maximal estimates for the triangle averaging operator
papers.abstract: Let $d\ge2$ and $t>0$. We study the bilinear triangle averaging operator $$\mathcal T_t(f,g)(x)=\int_{\mathcal I}f(x-ty)g(x-tz) d\sigma(y,z),$$ where $\sigma$ is the normalized surface measure on the manifold $\mathcal I=\{(y,z)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d:|y|=|z|=|y-z|=1\}$ of equilateral triangles of side length one with a vertex at the origin. We prove the strong-type asymmetric $L^p$-improving estimate $$\mathcal T_1:L^{\frac{d+1}{d-1}}(\mathbb R^d)\times L^{\frac{d^2-1}{d^2-3d+4}}(\mathbb R^d)\longrightarrow L^{\frac{d+1}{2}}(\mathbb R^d)$$ in every dimension $d\ge4$. This enlarges the range of exponents $(p,q,r)$ for which the triangle averaging operator is known to map $L^p(\mathbb R^d)\times L^q(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^r(\mathbb R^d)$, and symmetrization produces new symmetric estimates in every such dimension as well. The proof combines Sobolev smoothing estimates, obtained through a microlocal decomposition of the triangle incidence relation, with complex interpolation in an analytic family of averages over triangles of varying shape that contains the triangle averaging operator. We also establish maximal estimates for triangle averages. Let $E\subset[1,2]$ be a nonempty set of upper Minkowski dimension $\beta$, and let $\mathcal T_E(f,g)=\sup_{t\in E}|\mathcal T_t(f,g)|$. We prove that $$\|\mathcal T_E(f,g)\|_2\lesssim\|f\|_{H^{-s_1}}\|g\|_{H^{-s_2}}$$ whenever $s_1,s_2\ge0$, $s_1+s_2<\frac{d-3-\beta}{2}$ and $d>3+\beta$. This improves the previously known Sobolev smoothing estimate by half a derivative and lowers the dimension requirement. We also obtain asymmetric localized maximal estimates of the form $\mathcal T_E:L^p(\mathbb R^d)\times L^q(\mathbb R^d)\to L^r(\mathbb R^d)$ in an enlarged range of exponents.

papers.title: Parabolic Reifenberg Parametrizations and Corona Decompositions, with Applications to Singular Integrals
papers.abstract: For parabolic Ahlfors regular sets, we show that the bilateral weak geometric lemma (BWGL), bilateral approximation by unions of planes (BAUP), and corona decompositions by $Lip$(1,1/2) graphs (whose defining functions need not have half-order time derivatives in BMO) are equivalent. These geometric conditions do not imply the strong geometric lemma. A key tool is a parabolic version of Reifenberg's theorem for sets with holes, which we prove here. As an application of these geometric results, we prove that a parabolic Ahlfors $(n+2)$-regular measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, $1\leq n\leq d-1$, is parabolic uniformly rectifiable if its support satisfies any of these equivalent conditions and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(\mu)$.
